One caveat: the source provides only consolidated totals, so any effect of M&A or segment changes within FY2024 is embedded in the reported figures and cannot be isolated from this excerpt.

**Revenue growth, FY2023 → FY2024**

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | United Airlines Holdings | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.2%** [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Delta Air Lines | $58,048M | $61,643M | **+6.2%** [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest Airlines | $26,091M | $27,483M | **+5.3%** [DOC-1] |
| 5 | American Airlines Group | $52,788M | $54,211M | **+2.7%** [DOC-1] |

(United 6.23% vs. Delta 6.19% — effectively a tie, separated by ~4 basis points.)

**Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ revenue)**

| Rank | Airline | Op. income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta Air Lines | $5,995M | $61,643M | **9.7%** [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United Airlines Holdings | $5,096M | $57,063M | **8.9%** [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska Air Group | $570M | $11,735M | **4.9%** [DOC-1] |
| 4 | American Airlines Group | $2,614M | $54,211M | **4.8%** [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest Airlines | $321M | $27,483M | **1.2%** [DOC-1] |

(Alaska 4.86% vs. American 4.82% is also essentially a tie.)

**Conclusion:** No — the top-ranked airline differs. Alaska Air Group leads on revenue growth (+12.6%) but ranks only third on FY2024 operating margin (4.9%), while Delta leads on operating margin (9.7%) but ranks third on revenue growth (+6.2%) [DOC-1]. Notably, Alaska's fast top-line growth did not translate into leading profitability, and American posted revenue growth *and* the only decline in operating income among the five ($3,034M → $2,614M) [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Revenue growth: Alaska (+12.6%) > United (+6.2%) > Delta (+6.2%) > Southwest (+5.3%) > American (+2.7%). FY2024 operating margin: Delta (9.7%) > United (8.9%) > Alaska (4.9%) > American (4.8%) > Southwest (1.2%). No — Alaska tops revenue growth while Delta tops operating margin.
